newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh, Philippines to explore trade.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh, Philippines to explore trade.

text.p: Bangladesh and Philippine business leaders on Wednesday discussed ways to initiate trade and set up joint ventures, especially in textiles.
"We are interested particularly in textile, leather, ready-made garments and knit-wear," said Jose Juliano, Under-Secretary of the Philippine Department of Trade and Industry.
"...Bangladesh has no investment in Philippines and similarly we have no investment in Bangladesh."
Juliano is heading a 25-member business delegation accompanying Philippines President Fidel Ramos now on a three-day visit to Bangladesh.
Shafiqul Islam, Vice-President of the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry, said: "Composite textile is one of the attractive areas to investors from the Philippines.
"Bangladesh's garments industry has an annual requirement of over two billion metres of fabrics, which is mostly being met by imports," Islam said.
"We have been partners in trade for a long time but the volume of trade unfortunately has remained very low. The highest volume was $14 million in 1995-96."
Chemical fertilizer accounted for 93 percent of Bangladesh's $9 million exports to Philippines in 1995-6, against imports worth $5 million, mostly vegetable products.
